title: Prison unrest spread across Sri Lanka as rights group sought UN probe.
body_paragraphs: Letters to the resident coordinator detailed allegations of custodial deaths, assaults and denial of legal access after riots at several facilities. Two inmates died and dozens were hurt as officers used tear gas and reinforced perimeters.

Security forces, including elite units, were deployed to stabilise multiple sites while inquiries into organised criminal activity and drug links were opened. Administrators moved inmates back to cells and tightened controls around medical wings and gates.

title: A Bill was gazetted to extend superior court judges’ retirement ages and expand the appellate bench.
body_paragraphs: The draft law set new limits at 67 for the top court and 65 for the tier below, while raising the cap on appellate judges to 24. The Bar Association of Sri Lanka urged withdrawal, citing risks to judicial independence.

Legal arguments referenced a prior determination that changes affecting incumbents would trigger a referendum. A UN mandate holder also warned that altering tenure mid‑service could erode public confidence in impartial adjudication.

title: Colombo hosted ministerial talks with the European Union on investment climate and post‑2026 GSP+ (EU tariff‑preference scheme) access.
body_paragraphs: Participants reviewed an independent Investment Climate Assessment and discussed approval single windows, investor protection and customs and zone upgrades. The bloc’s envoys and local officials also weighed priorities for regulatory consistency.

With the current cycle ending on 31 December 2026, attention turned to transitional rules and later re‑application under expanded convention lists. The session closed with agreement to keep export preferences and the Global Gateway agenda central to near‑term work.

title: A national operation reviewed tougher sanctions for drug offences, including possible executions.
body_paragraphs: The Ratama Ekata council met under top leadership and ordered faster case handling by categorising seizures, while pushing coordination among analysts, prisons and police. Facilities reported the Welikada Prison gallows as operational, with two executioners on standby.

Officials said 806 inmates were on death row, including those convicted in narcotics cases, as religious leaders restated opposition to capital punishment. Debates highlighted the long‑standing moratorium (a formal suspension) and the trade risks of ending it.

title: Commercial‑scale battery systems were slated to connect to the grid in early September.
body_paragraphs: Installations at 16 electricity transmission substations neared completion, with the project near the Anuradhapura substation about 85% done. Each site will add 10 MW (megawatt) of storage to shift daytime solar and cut night‑time dispatch from diesel power plants.

title: Police said Red Notices had been obtained to trace 93 suspects abroad.
body_paragraphs: The global fugitive alerts helped return 38 suspects over recent years, with a further 35 repatriations arranged through the top cop’s office. Authorities also reported asset freezes worth Rs. 1.49 billion in 2024 and Rs. 1.549 billion in 2025 pending state acquisition.

title: Cabinet approved split awards for 2.28m tonnes of coal for the 2026/27 season.
body_paragraphs: Following nine bids, Aditya Birla Global Trading (Singapore) Pte. Ltd. received 70% of the award and Mohit Minerals Limited the remaining 30% to diversify supply risk. The contracts covered 1.596 million metric tonnes and 684,000 metric tonnes respectively for the Norochcholai plant.
bold_phrases: Aditya Birla Global Trading (Singapore) Pte. Ltd.

title: Cabinet cleared Rs. 1.2 billion for 21 expressway maintenance vehicles and machines.
body_paragraphs: The network spans 312 kilometres that have been in service for about a decade, with a further 92 kilometres due by 2027–2028. Funding will come from toll revenues as new links such as the Port Access Expressway and Central Expressway Section I open.

title: $2.73 million grant was approved for a three‑year nutrition project in four districts.
body_paragraphs: Backed by the Japan Social Development Fund of the World Bank Group, the programme will expand community services for pregnant and breastfeeding women and children under five. Work will target areas including Nuwara Eliya, Ratnapura, Polonnaruwa and Trincomalee.

title: A mobile hospital service for injured elephants was planned by wildlife authorities.
body_paragraphs: With support from the environment ministry, the scheme will speed treatment in remote areas while habitat work proceeds at sites such as Kalawewa and Tabbowa. Agencies also advanced village‑level electric fences and measures to curb train collisions.
